title: Fifth order finite volume WENO in general orthogonally-curvilinear coordinates
target_construct: Fifth order finite volume WENO reconstruction scheme for solving hyperbolic conservation equations in general orthogonally-curvilinear coordinates (Cartesian, cylindrical, spherical) on regularly- and irregularly-spaced grids.

findings.consequent: Achieves high order reconstruction in finite volume (FV) approach for hyperbolic conservation equations in orthogonally-curvilinear coordinates.
findings.validation_evidence: Demonstrated through analytical derivation and numerical tests.

components.name: Piecewise parabolic polynomial approximation
components.description: Used to reconstruct right, middle, and left interface values from zone averaged values (Qi).

components.name: Vandermonde-like linear system of equations
components.description: Inverted to recover grid dependent linear weights of the WENO scheme.

components.name: Linear weights
components.description: Grid dependent weights for reconstruction, derived from the Vandermonde-like system. Analytical values provided for standard uniform grids in Cartesian, cylindrical, and spherical coordinates.

components.name: Optimal weights
components.description: Weights that optimize the sum of lower order interpolated variables into a higher order accurate variable. Analytical values provided for standard uniform grids in Cartesian, cylindrical-radial, and spherical-radial coordinates.

components.name: Smoothness indicator (ISi,l)
components.description: Nonlinear tool to differentiate between smooth and discontinuous flows, derived from the L2-norm of derivatives of the reconstruction polynomial. A grid-independent relation is derived.

components.name: Nonlinear weights
components.description: Calculated using optimal weights and smoothness indicators to achieve high order accuracy and handle discontinuities.

components.name: Multi-dimensional extension
components.description: A computationally efficient extension to 2D and 3D domains, using one-point-at-boundary method for point value reconstruction.

components.name: Flux integration procedures
components.description: Procedures for integrating fluxes at interfaces, including specific Jacobians for different coordinate systems and averaging methods.

components.name: Source term integration procedures
components.description: Procedures for integrating source terms, considering point values and regularization for factors like '1/R'.

recommended_use: The fifth order finite volume WENO-C reconstruction scheme is recommended for achieving high order spatial accuracy with minimal computational cost in orthogonally-curvilinear coordinates (Cartesian, cylindrical, spherical) on both regularly-spaced and irregularly-spaced grids. It is suitable for solving hyperbolic conservation equations, including smooth and discontinuous flows, and can be extended to arbitrary order and multi-dimensions. It is stable with third or higher order Runge-Kutta time marching.
limitations: Analytical values of optimal weights for spherical-radial coordinates are highly intricate and contain high order terms, suggesting direct numerical operation after mesh generation.
Optimal weights are mirror-symmetric only for regularly-spaced Cartesian grids, implying non-symmetry for other coordinate systems.
For non-standard grids, direct integration of the Jacobian (∂V/∂ξ) is highly complex and time-consuming, requiring numerical integration and matrix inversion.
Analytical solutions for linear weights in spherical-meridional coordinates (θ) are highly complex, advising direct numerical inversion.
